runtime.q: Does it add a runtime dependency?
runtime.a: No. Your app keeps next-intl, i18next or FormatJS with plain JSON catalogs. glot works on the files, in your repo and in CI.

fails.q: What if the model keeps getting a string wrong?
fails.a: glot sends the exact reason back and retries twice, then tries the fallback model. If it still fails, nothing is written: the key is reported as rejected and stays untranslated.

code.q: Does my code leave my machine?
code.a: The strings to translate and their context go to your LLM provider. Not your source files. Nothing goes to glot's authors; there is no telemetry.

app.q: Do I need the web app?
app.a: No. The CLI and the MCP server do the whole job locally. The app adds a shared dashboard, review and GitHub sync for teams.

tools.q: Does it work with my tools?
tools.a: Websites built with Wix, Squarespace, Webflow, Shopify, WordPress and many others, web and mobile apps, emails and support tools. The integrations page has the full list.

google.q: Will Google show my translated pages?
google.a: Yes. Each language gets its own pages that search engines can read, with titles adapted to what people search for in each country.

privacy.q: What happens to my visitors' data?
privacy.a: glot counts visits without cookies or personal data. In emails and support messages, personal details are hidden before any AI sees the text.

price.a: You start for free, without a credit card. Paid plans add volume and the growth tools. And since glot is open source, you can also run it yourself.

oss.q: Is anything in the open-source tool limited?
oss.a: No. Quotas only apply to requests served by glot cloud. The CLI, the local MCP server and the GitHub Action never call the billing system.

byok.q: Do you mark up LLM costs?
byok.a: No. With your own key, you pay your LLM provider directly and glot neither counts nor marks up those translations. Without a key, the cloud can use glot's key: each plan includes a monthly amount, and monthly plans can continue beyond it with usage-based billing.

selfHost.a: Yes. The server is in the same MIT repository. Without Stripe keys, billing is off and every limit is lifted; you run and update it yourself.

limits.q: What happens when I reach a quota?
limits.a: The cloud endpoint answers 402 with a message and an upgrade link; your shipped catalogs keep working from your repository. Quotas reset on the 1st of each month (UTC).

tax.q: Are prices with or without VAT?
tax.a: Prices are shown without VAT. Stripe handles payments, invoices and VAT: VAT is added at checkout where it applies, and business customers can enter a VAT number. Invoices are in your billing settings.

quotas.a: Only what glot cloud serves: CDN/OTA requests, insights and experiment events, remote MCP calls, on-demand locale jobs, live review annotations and strings translated with glot's key. Live experiments and cloud projects count while they exist. Nothing you run locally, and nothing translated with your own key, is counted. Monthly counters reset on the 1st (UTC).

trial.q: Can I try Growth before paying?
trial.a: Yes. Your first Growth subscription starts with a 14-day free trial, once per account. Your payment method is saved at sign-up but nothing is charged before the trial ends; cancel before then from the billing portal and you pay nothing. Starter and Pro have no trial.

cancel.a: Yes, from the billing portal. Your plan stays active until the end of the period you paid for, then the account moves to Free. Projects and data are kept.

mock_output.fix: Nothing was pushed or synced. Check that the project uses a real AI provider with a valid key in Settings → LLM, then run again: placeholders are translated again.

ai_key_missing.fix: glot translates with your own AI provider key. Add it in Settings → LLM, click “Test the key”, then run again.

ai_quota.fix: Check your credit with the provider, or raise the budget in Settings → LLM, then run again. Translations already written are kept.

ai_unavailable.fix: Nothing is wrong on your side. Run again in a few minutes: translations already written are kept.

ai_workspace.cause: The Anthropic workspace does not match the key.
ai_workspace.fix: Organization keys (sk-ant-usr…) need the ID of their workspace (wrkspc_…). Set it in Settings → LLM, test the key, then run again.

branch_missing.cause: The base branch no longer exists in this repository.
branch_missing.fix: Choose the repository again and pick an existing branch.

config_invalid.cause: The glot.toml of this repository is not valid.
config_invalid.fix: Fix the line named in the technical details (paths must stay inside the repository) and push: glot runs again by itself.

no_framework.cause: glot did not find an app it can localize in this repository.
no_framework.fix: Supported: React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Leptos, SwiftUI and apps with their own t() function. In a monorepo, run glot init in the app folder, commit glot.toml and push.

pr_conflict.cause: A commit you pushed to the glot branch conflicts with the latest base branch.
pr_conflict.fix: Nothing was overwritten. Merge the base branch into the pull request and resolve the conflict, or close the pull request: glot opens a fresh one on the next run.

push_rejected.cause: GitHub refused the glot branch or its pull request.
push_rejected.fix: A branch protection rule probably covers glot/*. Allow the glot app to push to glot/* branches, then run again.

repo_access.cause: glot can no longer read this repository.
repo_access.fix: The GitHub App may have been uninstalled or lost access to this repository. Give it access again on GitHub, then run again.

repo_too_large.cause: This repository is larger than what one run can clone.
repo_too_large.fix: Media and files over 2 MB are already skipped. Move the app to its own repository, or contact us to raise the limit.

timeout.cause: The run took too long and was stopped.
timeout.fix: Run again: strings already translated are not redone. If it happens every time, narrow the scan with [extract] include in glot.toml.

unknown.cause: The run stopped on an unexpected error.
unknown.fix: Run again. If it fails the same way, send us the technical details below.

posthog.step1: In PostHog, open your avatar menu → Settings → Personal API keys → Create personal API key.
posthog.step2: Scope: Query → Read only (query:read), limited to this project.
posthog.step3: Project ID: Project settings → General → Project ID (a number).
posthog.step4: Region: US if you sign in at us.posthog.com, EU if at eu.posthog.com.
posthog.privacy: glot only asks PostHog for counts per day, browser language, page language and country. No person, IP address or URL is fetched. The key is stored encrypted and never shown again.

liveStream.title: Live stream
liveStream.subtitle: Translate text that does not exist yet: an AI answer, a notification, a chat message, while it streams, with your glossary and your translation memory.

optIn.title: This is your users' content
optIn.sent: What goes to your AI provider: the sentences to translate, the glossary terms they contain and the last sentences of the conversation. Code, links and do-not-translate terms are replaced by placeholders first; emails and long numbers (phones, cards) too unless you turn masking off. Names and postal addresses are not detected.
optIn.stored: What glot keeps: a keyed fingerprint and a counter per sentence, and daily totals. No text, unless you turn on the cache below.

mask_pii.label: Mask personal data
mask_pii.help: Emails and numbers of 7 digits or more never reach the provider; they are put back in the translation.

store.label: Cache translations
store.help: Keeps masked translations so a repeated sentence is instant and free. Turning it off deletes them.

browser.label: Browser access
browser.help: Accepts the project's public key from web pages. Off: your server only, with an API token.
